inspiration: Three-stage loot pick: a d100 gen-table row names an item table, a d320 roll (level-scaled for mobs) picks the item, then prefix and suffix mod tables each roll again (LootManager.java lines 138-200 and 202-265). Keep the base-plus-two-modifier shape; change the mod families and names.

Level-scaled roll window: the bottom of the window rises with mob level, the level is capped at 65 and the window tops out at 319 (TableRoll, LootManager.java lines 266-286). Keep the sliding window; change the curve. See the defect below.

Hot-zone bonus roll once per booty set: a normal roll, then one extra roll on the next table ID in a hot zone (RunBootySet, LootManager.java lines 98-136, line 125). Keep one bonus bite per encounter; change the +1 table convention to an explicit field.
Respawn gate per zone: one respawn per zone per 100 ms from a queue (MobRespawnThread.java lines 36-58; lines 42 and 51). Keep the rate limit; change the gate length and add a zone cap (row 23).

Race-filtered aggro: a mob skips player races on its not-enemy list, needs an enemy race when one is set, then checks range (MobAI.java lines 703-760). Keep the per-mob faction filter; change it to our factions, kept inside the engine.

Gold drop as chance then amount: a d100 check against a drop chance, then a random amount between two bounds (LootManager.java lines 289-302, grep-read only). Keep the two-number row shape; change the numbers.

DEFECT (keep the idea, fix the defect): at mob level 60 and above in a hot zone, the lower bound (LootManager.java line 276, plus the level from line 282) passes the 319 cap (lines 273-274), so nextInt(min, max + 1) gets an origin at or above its bound. Java's nextInt throws in that case (Java API behaviour, derived from the arithmetic, not executed). Fix: clamp min to max before the roll.

briefs.label: Hot-zone bonus draw
briefs.why: risky zones pay one extra chance without changing normal odds
briefs.keep: one bonus draw per encounter in a hot zone; the normal draw stays
briefs.change: an explicit bonus-table field; our own number; a zone-based name. Dom rule: a distinct original, never a copy

briefs.label: Mod-stacked item
briefs.why: the same base item looks different across drops, so drops feel personal
briefs.keep: independent prefix and suffix tables rolled on top of a base item
briefs.change: our naming and our mod families. Dom rule: a distinct original, never a copy

briefs.label: Zone respawn gate
briefs.why: a wiped zone refills at a readable pace instead of all at once
briefs.keep: one queue per zone and one spawn per gate interval
briefs.change: our gate length and a cap per zone type (row 23). Dom rule: a distinct original, never a copy

briefs.label: Level-window drop
briefs.why: higher-level enemies reward better items on a clear curve
briefs.keep: a roll window that slides up with level and is capped
briefs.change: a bounded shift and our own curve. Dom rule: a distinct original, never a copy

briefs.label: Race-filtered aggro
briefs.why: enemies ignore some kinds of player, so the world feels factional
briefs.keep: enemy and not-enemy lists per mob, checked before range
briefs.change: our factions and our hate list rules. Dom rule: a distinct original, never a copy
